reads_as_reason: Two plain near-parallel rounded slabs with a hard angled cut at the shank top and no knee form; a blank shell, though the surface finish is clean.

G1.evidence: Thigh is a rounded-rectangle slab with near-parallel sides and a blunt distal cap; nothing marks the knee; a placeholder block. P8a 0.708 and P8b 0.712 fail.

G2.evidence: Thigh ends in a rounded cap and the shank begins with a flat diagonal slice: a half-disc face with a hard line in the back view, a knife edge in the side view. The front outline is a continuous curve (S3a 0).

G3.evidence: No colour; no secondary feature that a dark/light split could attach to apart from the parting line and the knee gap.

G4.evidence: Same squarish section and corner-radius family, matching end caps and rounded edges; the exception is the sharp shank-top cut, covered under G2.

G6.evidence: No references. Optimus / Atlas show a knee actuator mass, clear taper and panel breaks; here near-constant-width slabs, so a weak match.

pairwise.evidence: Silhouettes and knee cut are visually identical in both sheets, so the preference rests on surface quality. The candidate's zebra stripes are smooth continuous bands wrapping the end caps; the baseline's zebra is fragmented noisy blobs with blotchy contour islands. Its large white zebra fields match the failed S4a (0.4341). Moderate preference.

top_changes.change: Remove the knife edge and flat half-disc at the shank top; fillet the proximal edge so the gap reads as a deliberate recess.
More shank taper (P8b 0.712) and lower mid-section squareness to cut flat share (S4a 0.4341).

notes: Round 2. The zebra views were the only strong differentiator; the target matches almost perfectly (T1 0.9887 / 0.9862), which says the design matches its target, not that the target looks finished.
